title: Format Titan's P&L Like a Mumbai Desk Analyst
scenario: You've pulled Titan Company's FY23–FY24 P&L from the NSE filing, raw and unformatted. Your senior has asked you to rebuild it following the desk's formatting code: colour-coded inputs (blue) and formulas (black), right-aligned ₹ cr figures with Indian commas, proper borders, frozen headers, and grouped detail rows. The model must be audit-ready and printable within 90 seconds of opening.
instructions: Apply analyst formatting to the raw P&L data: format all currency values as ₹ crore with Indian comma separators, colour inputs blue and formulas black, freeze the header row, add hierarchy indents and group detail rows, border subtotals and totals, and verify all column widths are readable. Then answer five questions about the formatted sheet's structure and the unit-conversion logic underlying it.
learning_objective: Apply colour-coding (blue inputs, black formulas, green cross-sheet links), currency formatting (₹ crore with lakhs-style commas), alignment rules (right-align numbers, indent hierarchy), borders (punctuation not fencing), and freeze/group controls to a financial statement, and execute unit conversions (₹ to ₹ cr) without error.
hints: The colour code is a safety system: blue = typed by a human, black = calculated by a formula. Use Home → Font Color to colour cells after you format their numbers.

To apply Indian comma separators (12,34,567 style), use Ctrl+1 → Custom and paste the code `[>=10000000]##\,##\,##\,##0;[>=100000]##\,##\,##0;##,##0`. Or use the pre-built Accounting format and manually adjust the thousands separator in the Custom category.

For the conversion questions: 1 crore = 1,00,00,000 (seven zeros); 1 crore = 100 lakhs; 1 crore = 10 millions. A cell showing ₹5,07,890 lakh is 5,07,890 ÷ 100 = ₹5,079 crore. Always check the header label to confirm the unit before you calculate.

A2.value: Q1: What is the EBITDA Margin for FY24 (EBITDA ÷ Revenue, as %)? Format as number with 2 decimals.

A3.value: Q2: Revenue growth from FY23 to FY24 in absolute ₹ crore. (Use a formula: FY24 revenue minus FY23 revenue.)

A4.value: Q3: If Titan's FY24 revenue were expressed in ₹ lakh instead of ₹ crore, what would the figure be? (Multiply by 100.)

A5.value: Q4: EBIT margin for FY24, as a percentage of Revenue. (EBIT ÷ Revenue × 100, formatted to 1 decimal.)

A6.value: Q5: Cost of Materials as a % of Revenue, FY24. (COGS ÷ Revenue × 100, formatted to 1 decimal.)
